shared_elements: low-relief carving on a stone slab/panel
horizontal band of repeated geometric pattern crossing the upper part of the field
a row of repeated small figures along the top edge
division of the surface into stacked registers/zones
framing or border element along an edge
justification: The most specific correspondence is that both slabs carry a horizontal band of repeated geometric ornament across the upper field with a row of small repeated figures above it and larger profile creatures below, so both are register-organised relief panels. Against this, A is a dense, all-over curvilinear composition of seated human figures, foliage and glyph-like motifs filling every space within a scrolled border, whereas B is a sparse, flat-relief arrangement of isolated animals on a blank ground, with no human figures and no framing scrollwork — the manner of rendering shares little beyond both being carved stone.
